title: biRISC-V (ultraembedded/biriscv)
_note: The dual-issue superscalar RV32IMZicsr core: core, instruction / data caches,
tightly-coupled memory and the two tops (riscv_top with caches, riscv_tcm_top).
biriscv_xilinx_2r1w wraps the Xilinx RAM16X1D primitive the repository does not define; excluded with it.
biriscv_fetch uses the PRIV_* macros of src/core/biriscv_defs.v without including it (the FuseSoC core compiles the defs file first): always_srcs puts it in every closure.
First local sweep 2026-10-26 (44 rows): 28 / 40 comparable proven, 37 / 40
elaborate, 0 undriven, every co-simulated row PASS.  Left: 6 SAT-budget rows
(the multiplier, the register file, the caches’ RAMs and riscv_tcm_top, which
runs over the memory cap), 3 rows whose miter cannot run (the two single-port
RAM wrappers reach a $mem_v2 satgen has no model for, biriscv_trace_sim is
simulation-only), 4 rows without a read_slang reference (it rejects biRISC-V’s
use-before-declaration in the caches), and four `differs` rows -- biriscv_exec,
_frontend, _npc and dcache_core_tag_ram -- all with a clean co-simulation: the
branch-predictor leads tracked from the first sweep.
First NIGHTLY 2026-10-27 (run 40480115156): 28 / 44 proven, 42 / 43 co-sim
pass, 44 / 44 opt-clean with 0 undriven, 7 rows not comparable -- and ONE
read_uhdm co-simulated divergence with read_slang CLEAN, so unlike NVDLA's
70 this one IS adjudicated and is a genuine reader lead.  It sits beside the
four `differs` rows already tracked above (biriscv_exec, _frontend, _npc,
dcache_core_tag_ram), two of which -- _exec and _npc -- were re-measured
against main on 2026-10-27 and still differ with a clean co-simulation.
